title: Research: desktop first
detail: Phone keyboards cannot see the screen, but on a Mac one app can read the field you are in and type into any other. So Foretype starts on the Mac, with a plan a second reviewer checked.

title: Landing site live
detail: Two designs built side by side, merged into the one you are reading, with this build log fed straight from the repository.

title: Feasibility proven: Accessibility + on-device model
detail: Suggestions appear at the cursor and drop in with Tab in TextEdit, Notes, Safari, Chrome and Slack. A small model on the Mac offers the first word in about 7 ms, and 18 of 20 test replies were good enough to keep.

title: App skeleton with frozen contracts
detail: The menu-bar app, the model engine and the Mac plumbing now share one fixed set of shapes, so each part can be built and tested on its own.

title: Guardrails: rules, checks and CI
detail: Every change is formatted, linted, scanned for secrets and built and tested on a Mac before it lands. A privacy check keeps the app off the network, apart from the one model download.

title: Open source: repo public
detail: The code, the plan and the research notes are public on GitHub under the MIT license, with guides for anyone who wants to help.

title: The Mac app, end to end
detail: Filling in the skeleton: reading the field, suggesting, showing the grey text and inserting it, then a first build you can download.

title: An Android keyboard
detail: The same on-device model inside a keyboard of its own, so sloppy swipes and taps still land on the word you meant.
